pages.text: "I'll move it all myself!" Sharp-eared deer Mumu tugged a huge palm leaf lying in the middle of the village road. It did not budge.
"It will make a seat under the well tree!" Mumu pulled again. The leaf was much longer than Mumu. Even walking backward left it in the same place.
Chickens hurried over and hopped onto the leaf. Mumu's ears turned toward them. Now it was heavier. Mumu sweated, but the leaf did not move even a handspan.
Quick-handed monkey Taro ran over. "I'll hold it, too!" Mumu shook their head. "I can do it." Taro caught the opposite end. "No one's lifting here."
"Lift only one end, and the other stays on the ground." Taro raised the front. "Me in Front, You Behind—Heave-Ho!" Mumu lifted the back, and the leaf rose.
The chickens clucked and tumbled off. Taro tapped twice with his branch to set the rhythm. "Me in Front, You Behind—Heave-Ho!" The leaf slid along the road.
Without a rest, they reached the well tree and spread the leaf on the ground. "With two of us, it's not heavy at all!" Mumu said.
They sat together on the wide leaf that had not moved when pulled alone. The chickens climbed back onto its edge.

This was how to move heavy things: one, call if I can't do it alone! Two, one in front and one behind! Three, say heave-ho together! Even pushing a big tub beneath the porch, they matched their voices.

Mumu sat close, leaning a shoulder against Taro. What would not move for one grew light for two. "Me in Front, You Behind—Heave-Ho! Now we can move anything!" One of Mumu's ears slipped over Taro's head.
